newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek minister to attend Albania peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Greek minister to attend Albania peace talks.

text.p: Greek Deputy Foreign Minister Yannos Kranidiotis plans to join shipboard talks in the Adriatic aimed at ending the violence in Albania, the foreign ministry said on Friday.
Greece is gravely concerned with the crisis just across its northern border.

A foreign ministry spokeswoman said Kranidiotis had flown to the Italian port of Brindisi and will go aboard the warship Aliseo to attend the meeting of Albania's government, the insurgents and European mediator Franz Vranitzky.
Vranitzky began talks with Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino aboard the Italian frigate earlier on Friday.
The Greek frigate "Kavaloudis" evacuated 49 people -- 44 Greeks and five Belgians -- from the Albanian port of Durres, west of Tirana, on Friday, defence ministry officials said.
Three more Greek navy ships were in the area in case further evacuations are necessary. A plan to send an air force cargo plane to Tirana was abandoned because the city's airport was closed.

There are about 30 Greek diplomats in Tirana and an army of Greek reporters both in the capital and southern Albania, now mostly controlled by insurgents armed with weapons looted from military depots.
